t: You are on Langham Place, a short street just north of Oxford Circus. It connects Portland Place to the north with Regent Street to the south. It has been home to many significant public buildings, and it gives its name to the Langham Place Group, a circle of early women's rights activists. Nevil Maskelyne, the British magician and inventor, died here in 1924. The chemist, cleric and writer John Marks Ashley was born here, and the art collector Adrian Hope died here in 1863.
